title: How special pool catches bugs
hints: Place the block at the end of its page: then "past the end" and "on the guard page" are the same thing, and the fill pattern sits in front of the block where underruns land.
Do not erase freed blocks from the map: keeping them, marked as freed, is what lets you tell a use-after-free or double free from an unknown handle.
requirements: Overruns are caught on the very first byte past the block, for reads and writes.
Underruns are caught when the block is freed.
Freed memory can no longer be read or written, and double frees and tag mismatches are reported.
Leaks are reported by tag at unload.
stretch: Add the other half of special pool: an option to place blocks at the **start** of the page with the guard page before it, which catches underruns at once instead of at free (and misses overruns), and pick the mode per allocation tag.
